8b.prompt: These are two crops from the same NBHL ball-hockey recording. Compare the central player in image A with the central player in image B. Decide whether visible evidence establishes the same individual, establishes different individuals, or is insufficient. Team uniform or similar appearance alone does not establish the same individual. Use same only for a clearly matching complete jersey number with consistent uniform, or a distinctive matching combination of equipment that distinguishes this player from teammates. Use different for a clear contradiction such as opposing uniforms, field player versus goalie equipment, clearly different complete jersey numbers, or clearly different distinctive equipment. Consider blur, occlusion, lighting and viewing direction before treating a feature as a contradiction. Do not invent hidden digits or assume an automatic track is correct. Read a number only if all its digits are clearly visible on the central player; otherwise use null. If one central person cannot be isolated, use uncertain. Return only JSON: {"identity":"same, different, or uncertain", "number_a":integer or null, "number_b":integer or null, "evidence":"short specific visible agreement, contradiction, or uncertainty"}.
8b.scope: Post-audit development diagnostic on selected long-track hypotheses, not a fresh or representative MOT test.

scope: Post-audit development comparison on the same reviewed endpoints within each sampling set. Sources and sampling sets remain separate.
limitations: Assistant review, not independent human ground truth. The 82 BoT-SORT and 34 SAM2 positive hypotheses have different selection distributions; their aggregate precision is not a fair algorithm comparison. Unknown identities do not enter accuracy. Missing observations are separate from rejected matches. The long SAM2 run only covers 600–720 source seconds. Pair decisions do not establish identity throughout the intervening video or full-game statistics.
